record.original_question: Give rigorous derivations of one-dimensional rod models and two-dimensional plate or shell models from three-dimensional elasticity, proving that their solutions approximate appropriate three-dimensional elastic solutions as the thickness parameter h tends to zero, with convergence and error estimates that handle loads, boundary conditions, buckling, and boundary layers.

evidence.quote: Problem 18. Give a rigorous derivation of models of rods, plates and shells, showing that their solutions well approximate appropriate solutions to three-dimensional elasticity for small values of the thickness parameter h.
one would ideally like results showing that the solution sets for boundary-value value problems of three-dimensional elasticity converge as h → 0

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega_h = \omega \times (-h/2, h/2) \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ for a bounded Lipschitz domain $\omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ (or, for rods, let $\Omega_h$ be a thin tube of cross-sectional diameter $h$ around a smooth curve in $\mathbb{R}^3$). Consider three-dimensional hyperelastic bodies governed by a stored-energy functional
$$E_h(y) = \int_{\Omega_h} W(\nabla y(x))\, dx - \int_{\Omega_h} f_h \cdot y\, dx - \int_{\partial_N \Omega_h} g_h \cdot y\, dS,$$
where $W : \mathbb{R}^{3\times 3} \to [0,\infty]$ is a frame-indifferent stored-energy density satisfying $W(R) = 0$ for $R \in SO(3)$, $W(F) \ge c\,\mathrm{dist}^2(F, SO(3))$, and is suitably regular near $SO(3)$; deformations $y : \Omega_h \to \mathbb{R}^3$ are subject to mixed Dirichlet/Neumann boundary conditions on the lateral and end (or top/bottom) faces of $\Omega_h$, and $f_h, g_h$ are applied body and surface loads.

(a) Rigorously derive one-dimensional rod models and two-dimensional plate and shell models as the limits of $E_h$ when the thickness parameter $h \to 0$, for all natural scalings of the elastic energy (e.g., $h^\beta$-scalings yielding stretching, von Kármán, linearized von Kármán, bending, and constrained membrane regimes).

(b) Prove that, for each such regime, the sets of (approximate) minimizers and, more generally, solution sets of the corresponding three-dimensional boundary value problems converge — in a suitable topology after rescaling to a fixed reference domain — to the solution sets of the limit lower-dimensional models, with quantitative error estimates in $h$.

(c) Extend these convergence and error results to handle:
  (i) general dead and live loads and mixed boundary conditions;
  (ii) buckling phenomena, including bifurcation diagrams of the 3D problem versus those of the reduced model;
  (iii) boundary layers near lateral boundaries and points of boundary-condition change.

Give a unified rigorous theory establishing such derivations together with explicit convergence and error estimates that cover (a), (b), and (c).
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on this program. Via Γ-convergence, a complete hierarchy of plate models (membrane, von Kármán, linearized von Kármán, bending/Kirchhoff) has been rigorously derived from 3D nonlinear elasticity (Friesecke–James–Müller and successors), as well as analogous theories for rods (including bending–torsion, curved, and incompressible rods) and shells (nonlinear bending shells, von Kármán shells, homogenized shells). However, a unified theory delivering quantitative error estimates, convergence of full solution sets (not just minimizers) under general loads and mixed boundary conditions, rigorous treatment of buckling/bifurcation, and complete boundary-layer analysis remains incomplete; many of these aspects are still active research problems.
